id:2123278949749059756.text:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped from agents that spit out a quick answer for you, to today agents that you orchestrate inside of a set of tasks. But as agents can both fan out and work in parallel, handle much larger context, be able to do long running work, and have far greater levels of capabilities, we’re entering yet another level of what we can have AI do for us.

We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents. 

But the impact can be quite massive across the rest of knowledge work. You’ll tell an agent to improve your client onboarding workflow to achieve a certain targeted goal; or have agents go reduce risk in your business; or improve your security posture on an ongoing basis.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. Importantly, this leads to outcomes and results that humans literally couldn’t have accomplished before. This will lead to fairly new levels of productivity with AI.

id:2123686350410912145.text:
This year we’ve had a clear jump in model capability where instead of telling agents precisely what to do, it’s better to use these systems to solve problems you can’t easily define yourself. 

A year ago you’d need to very clearly tell agents the how to design and develop your product idea, or there was almost no chance of success. Now, increasingly, the agent likely can come up with a better implementation than you’d have thought of because you can have it connect the dots between a far greater solution space than you can. 

This will be increasingly true in basically every domain of kneeler work. We’re going to see this impact in finance, legal, life sciences, cyber, and many other spaces where no person can hold onto all the available relevant industry knowledge to think of the best solution. 

Ultimately this is going to reshape our relationship with AI and how we deploy agents in our work. It won’t be about explicitly telling them, but instead giving them goals and enough freedom to pursue them in the best way they can.

id:2123426647273800172.text:
As these network attacks and impersonation attempts happen, who's securing the elderly? 

Especially thinking about my parents and grandparents.

There are four layers I can think through where this could work.

One is at the browser level, where somebody builds a secure browser that ensures that whatever websites they're going to are secured. Texts typically lead to a link, even for payments. This is why browser is key.

Two could be at the network layer, where there is a physical device, similar to Pi-hole, or an Onavo-like VPN on your phone, that blocks websites that could be deemed unsafe.

Three could be at the payments layer, where transactions that look like scams get flagged before the money leaves.

And fourth and most crazy could be at the phone level, where everything is monitored, and you're only getting calls from your loved ones. Cloned voices would work with a provider like Reality Defender. 

There are individual solutions for this today but none neatly packaged. 

This could all be packaged with insurance that covers any activities on the OS or phone. In that way, incentives are aligned to keep this on the edge.

The buyer would be the kids, someone like me, who get alerted when something looks off.

I’m being pitched a new inference neocloud company on average every two days. No exaggeration. I take every entrepreneur seriously and I look deeply into each.

But it’s hard to fathom this being sustainable. At the same time, AI Gateway token demand on Vercel has been ~40% MoM compounded since the beginning of the year. No signs of stopping.

One way to reconcile this is that compute is the new economy, and tokens the new energy unit. There’s a new Industrial Revolution taking place. Every aspect of our lives is being replatformed on top of this new system that enhances everything. More like an “oil rush” than a “gold rush”: it’s durable, not a fad.

In the short term, I anticipate more expansion, followed by consolidation due to economies of scale, cybersecurity and enterprise requirements (ZDR and cyber being a hot topic for inference providers), capital requirements, and an evolving regulatory landscape.

id:2123237505810178434.text:
One of the most impressive things I've seen, and I think this is an important advancement to the state of the art.

Message boards were the enabling technology of both the Navier-Stokes math breakthrough and even the OpenAI/HuggingFace cyber feat.

We built a message board infrastructure primitive. You can think of it as "headless Slack" (or remember IRC?) for agents.

This is an important building block for software factories, self-optimizing systems, and scientific research, where the human prompting is just the seed of the system, and millions of agents can operate in a decentralized fashion.

𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚋𝚘𝚊𝚛𝚍 is designed to be model, harness and hosting platform agnostic. Just bring your agents, give them our CLI, and watch magic happen.

id:2123468825538789380.text:
𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚋𝚘𝚊𝚛𝚍 has no heavyweight or opinionated UI. It's infra not product. I love the "headless Slack" for agents analogy, because UI is free now.

You can generate and deploy the ideal "factory interface" for each usecase. A security team will focus on vulnerability counts, SEV classifications, confirmed vs unconfirmed.

I've seen internal factories at Vercel built on Board that are just TUIs. Or mostly managed via a Slack agent, and you just focus on the outcomes and giving feedback to the agents. 

The board is like the Redux state manager of your agents. It's foundational.

id:2122746401482592549.text:
devin bots are multi-agent teams done right:
- always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI)
- own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others)
- manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself)
- available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction)
- consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212)

this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god)

hyped concepts this replaces:
- /goal
- "ultracode" / "ultra mode"
- "loop engineering"
- "agent to agent"
- "agent swarms"
- AI employees (see below)

my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes. 

incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol.

if youre a startup, reminder that Devin for Startups offers 65k in credits. apply via clanker

id:2122929634916679820.text:
One of the funny reasons for the difference in vibes between the influencers and the crowd today on 6.2 Sol/Astra is that we gave a few folks access a while ago and then made a lot of changes in the last 3-4 days and I'm pretty sure no re-testing was done within those days and the videos were produced last week.

Don't get me wrong, while the models are a hefty jump compared to their GPT predecessors, they are by no means perfect and there are a few things the teams are excited for the models to get better at in future iterations in terms of taste and niceness of use. Love all the feedback and we hear you!

id:2122929829863735594.text: If you have Pro 200/500, I do recommend trying out 6.2 Sol ultrafast, it's quite the blast to use and a completely different feel. I'm excited to keep pushing in bringing these speeds to more users over time.

We’re also working on a new mobile experience for ChatGPT! 

It’s easier to get to your favorite features and discover what you can do in ChatGPT. We’re starting with Pro users who have a dot or are eligible to create one. Your dot gets its own tab, and you can pin Codex, Projects, Images, and more to the tab bar. Some of you will see the new experience by default. 

You can turn it on or off anytime in Settings > New ChatGPT Design. 

Super excited to hear your feedback before we roll it out more widely!
